q: Your budget alert at 100% arrives by email. What has happened to the app?
why: Alerts only notify; they never stop spending, and billing data arrives with a delay.

q: The Notes home screen lists notes with no limit(). What happens to reads as users write more notes?
why: Each returned document is a read, so an unbounded query costs more every month. Add limit() and paginate.

q: A function runs on each write to a note and updates that same note. What goes wrong?
o: It triggers itself in a loop
why: Each update is a new write that starts the function again. Exit early when nothing changed.

q: You want spending to stop by itself at a limit. What does disabling billing by code cost you?
o: All services stop; data may be lost
why: Removing the billing account shuts down every service in the project, and resources might be deleted for good.

q: One screen reads 20 notes per open, opened 5 times a day by 1,000 users. Reads per day?
why: 1,000 x 5 x 20 = 100,000 reads; subtract the free daily quota to find billable reads.

q: Which item is a real pre-launch risk?
o: The web apiKey in the app
A service-account key in the repo
Budget alerts to a team inbox
why: A service-account key gives full admin access. The web config is not a secret.

q: Moving to Blaze removes the free quotas, so a small app suddenly costs money.
why: Blaze keeps the free quotas and charges only for usage above them.

q: You can export your users, but password hashes use Firebase's own scrypt variant, so the new system must support it or users reset passwords.
why: firebase auth:export includes the hashes; importing them elsewhere needs the hash settings and support for that variant.
